description: We are Team Aether for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge! We focus on web development, UI design, generative AI, AI, satellite communications, hardware design, and low-cost innovative ideas. Join us to build an impactful space project!
summary: NASA's Solar System Relics is an interactive digital museum bringing six decades of Moon and Mars exploration to life for young learners. Profiling thirteen historic NASA spacecraft—from Ranger 7 and Surveyor 3 to Apollo 11, Opportunity, and Ingenuity—our platform combines an interactive planetary coordinate map with collectible, Topps-style infographic cards. Students explore real archival photography, blueprints, mission lifetimes, power systems, and budgets before interviewing each spacecraft through an AI-powered first-person chat grounded in official NASA logs. Powered by NSSDCA, LROC, and HiRISE open data, we ensure humanity’s pioneering off-world hardware is never forgotten.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Echoes of the Frontier: NASA's Solar System Relics is an interactive digital museum introducing school-age students (ages 10–16) to 13 historic NASA spacecraft resting on the Moon and Mars—from Ranger 7 (1964) and Apollo 11 (1969) to Opportunity and Ingenuity (2024).

  • Interactive Coordinate Map: Users switch between Lunar and Martian surface maps with clickable pins plotted at real landing coordinates.
  • Collectible Infographic Cards: Each artifact features a Topps-style card with 4 visual views (Surface, Blueprint, Orbital, and Discovery) plus key metrics (Mission Lifetime, Power Source, Budget, and Status).
  • "Talk to Spacecraft" AI Chat: Students interview each lander or rover in first-person character via a Gemini-powered chat drawer grounded in real NASA mission logs.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessible STEM Storytelling: Turns dense technical archives into engaging visual infographics and conversations for younger learners.
  • Real Engineering Context: Highlights how budgets, power systems, and lifespans shape space exploration, inspiring excitement for future Artemis missions.

Tools, Languages & Data Used

  • Tech Stack: React, TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide icons, built and deployed via Google AI Studio with the Gemini API.
  • NASA Open Data: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO HiRISE).

Creativity & Key Design Factors

  • Creative Approach: Blends collectible trading-card aesthetics with emotional first-person spacecraft personas so silent hardware feels alive.
  • Key Factors Considered: Zero-login browser accessibility, Light/Dark mode readability for classrooms, and strict factual accuracy verified against official NASA records.
